Chapter 9  Pulmonary Disease 
381
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Chapter 9: Case 2)
Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is defined as recurrent episodes of apnea during sleep caused by 
occlusion of the upper airway. Obesity is the primary risk factor for OSA and is present in up to 
two-thirds of all patients with OSA. OSA may be caused by an increased amount of fat surrounding 
the structures of the upper airway. Although not all obese patients have OSA, and occasional non-
obese patients may have it, it is clear that weight loss in obese patients with OSA improves signs 
and symptoms. Symptoms of sleep apnea, such as snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness, should 
always be ascertained as part of the medical history in obese patients.
Two groups of inflammatory proteins are produced and released by adipose tissue: cytokines, 
such as TNF-α and adipokines, such as leptin. These cytokines may play a role in the development 
of insulin resistance and increased oxidative stress in obese patients.
